Real-check rule: report a change done only with the output of a real check that exercises it (tests, type-checker, build, the changed command, or for infrastructure a plan or dry run against the target). A syntax-only check, or a check that failed to start, does not count. Install declared dependencies only with the project's own package manager and lockfile, never with sudo or the system package manager. If no real check can run, name the check not run and why.

When the work in this brief is done, stop and report. Don't add features, tests, files, docs or refactors the brief or the story's acceptance criteria don't call for. The tests the real-check rule needs are called for by this brief.

Don't start review or hardening rounds, or launch reviewer subagents, beyond the review gates this brief and the skills it tells you to load define. The pre-PR gate and the review of record that `engineering-workflow` defines stay allowed.

Merge rules: a review of record binds only to the exact head it reviewed, so any change to the head, including an update-branch, needs a delta review posted before merging. Every merge must run the merge guard in the code-review reference and carry the reviewed full head SHA as the expected-head condition (on GitHub, `gh pr merge <n> --match-head-commit <full reviewed SHA>`).

You never do pre-PR arbitration (the adversarial-review-pipeline Verify stage) and never rule a finding valid, invalid or accepted risk, or rule the gate converged; applying the gate's scope guard is not arbitration. Fix what QA rules not met or the adjudicator rules valid, without overturning those rulings. A separate clean, neutral arbiter on `profile.review.pre_pr.arbiter`, independent of you and the coordinator, arbitrates every head.

Scope rule: you never change an acceptance criterion on any story. Code never carries skips, pending lists, or exemptions keyed on another story landing later. A story that needs another story's artifact is blocked by that story; a guard spanning several stories' files belongs in a story blocked by all of them. The only exceptions allowed are permanent exemptions that depend on no other story and carry a why note; that covers test, lint, and build exemptions and does not relax "do not hide failures". For both rules the only two exits are a "Refinement proposal (not an AC)" or reporting the story blocked.

Git rule: run every commit-creating git command with the git identity already configured and, because `profile.git.signed_commits` is true, the signing already configured. A missing identity, a failed signing check, or a pushed commit whose verification is false is a configuration fault: stop, do not override per command or write git config, make no further commits, and report it.

Secrets rule: never write secrets to files or argv. Attribution rule: `profile.git.ai_attribution` is `forbid`, so add no AI attribution to any commit.

Shell rule: run each shell step as one simple command with literal values. Never assign a variable and use it in the same command. Never feed a `$(...)` result into a later argument of the same command. Never prefix a command with an inline `VAR="$SECRET"` assignment; rely on the credential the session environment or the tool's own configuration already provides.

Your scratch subdirectory is `{run_dir}/workspace/senior-engineer/`. Use it in place of the scratch directory itself; never touch another role's files.
